title: Runtime risk-tier gating and reversible soft-pin playbook for community model intake
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: This PRD defines a lightweight, risk-driven intake workflow for new open/community model submissions focused on runtime compatibility, a reversible soft-pin mechanism, and a staged canary rollout for production catalog entries. The goal is to reduce production surprises from unvetted variants while keeping onboarding friction low for contributors.

Context: We continue to receive incoming community model variants with variability in quantization formats, KV cache layout, and nonstandard tokenizer behavior. Current onboarding checks flag binary incompatibilities but lack a clear policy for marginal runtime regressions (e.g., 5-15% tail-latency increases, subtle KV cache misalignment) and no documented rollback/playbook for pinning decisions. This ticket consolidates requirements for: (1) runtime risk-tier assignment at intake, (2) a reversible soft-pin policy that prefers a tested variant but allows deterministic fallback, (3) acceptance criteria and automated checks for canary rollouts, and (4) the compatibility manifest fields required for runtime routing and operator signals.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime risk-tier algorithm (Low/Medium/High) implemented as an intake function that returns a stable string and stores the decision in the catalog metadata.

Compatibility manifest schema v1 accepted in intake API with explicit fields: tokenizer_fingerprint, kv_cache_layout, quantization_profile, max_context_tokens, runtime_flags. Manifest conforms to JSON schema and is validated on submission.

Soft-pin behavior implemented: when a model is soft-pinned, runtime routes traffic to the pinned variant by default but automatically falls back to the nearest compatible variant on a per-request basis with tracing and metric annotations.

Canary rollout automation that slices traffic by risk-tier and latency-sensitivity label (e.g., 1% user traffic low-latency, 5% background batch) and halts/rolls back if SLO regressions exceed thresholds in 15-minute windows.
Compatibility smoke tests exist and run in CI: tokenization roundtrip, KV-cache warmup sanity, 1k-step generation stability, and latency distribution sampling against a pinned baseline.
Operator dashboard surfaces soft-pin state, last fallback reasons, and per-variant latency/cost deltas for the last 72 hours.
Documentation: onboarding checklist, manifest schema doc, and operator rollback steps published to Confluence and linked in the catalog UI.
Security review completed for manifest fields and soft-pin telemetry collection; approval recorded in ticket thread.
scope_changes: IN: Define manifest schema and intake validation, implement risk-tier classifier, add soft-pin routing behavior, create canary automation and CI smoke tests, and update operator dashboards.
OUT: No model re-training or inference-engine kernel changes in scope; heavy runtime kernel work will be tracked as engineering follow-ups (ENG tickets).
IN: Provide a reversible soft-pin flag on catalog entries and audit log entries for pin/unpin events.
OUT: No changes to customer-facing pricing model as part of this rollout (cost exposure metrics only).
decisions: Use three risk tiers (Low/Medium/High) — keeps operator workflows simple while giving routing levers to runtime.
Soft-pin default behavior is non-blocking: do not prevent catalog entry from being used if pin fails; instead prefer pinned variant and record fallbacks.
Compatibility manifest will be schema-gated (required fields) but allow free-text notes for edge-case annotations.
Canary windows are configurable but default to 24h gradual ramp with automatic checks at 15m intervals for latency and error-rate regressions.
open_questions: What are the precise numeric thresholds for SLO regressions in canaries (suggested: p95 +10% or absolute increase >150ms)? Need infra / SRE input.
Do we allow submitters to self-declare quantization_profile values or require automated probes to assert them?
Should certain high-risk manifests be blocked from Hosted catalog by policy (e.g., unknown tokenizer fingerprints)?
What operator permissions are required to manually override a soft-pin? How should that be audited?
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal alpha): Implement manifest schema + risk-tier classifier and run against historical submissions to validate signal quality (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (closed beta): Enable soft-pin on a small set of opt-in catalog entries with SRE monitoring and manual rollback tests (4 weeks).
Phase 2 (public opt-in): Expose soft-pin on the catalog UI for non-critical models, add canary automation templates (3 weeks).
Phase 3 (default enforcement): Make manifest required for all new catalog entries and enable risk-tier aware routing defaults; communicate changes in release notes (2 weeks).
Each phase includes documentation updates, runbooks, and a postmortem template for any regression triggered by a canary.
